# find_missing_game_metadata

[← Command index](README.md)

Find games whose Pegasus metadata entries are missing fields.

## Synopsis

```
find_missing_game_metadata [options]
```

## Description

Reads every Pegasus metadata file in the game metadata repository and checks each
entry for the fields chosen with `-k`. A field counts as missing when it is absent or
empty.

`Minimum` checks game, platform and file. `Downloadable` checks the fields that
`build_game_metadata_files` can fetch: description, genre, coop, developer, publisher,
players and release. `All` checks every metadata field.

The log shows the entry count and, per field, how many entries lack it. Each non-empty
list is written in full to `Missing_<field>.txt` in the current directory, one
`<platform> - <game>` per line.

## Options

### General

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-k, --keys <Minimum\|Downloadable\|All>` | Which set of metadata fields to check. Default: `Downloadable`. Allowed: `Minimum`, `Downloadable`, `All`. |

### Common options

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-v, --verbose` | Enable verbose mode. |
| `-p, --pretend_run` | Do a pretend run with no permanent changes. |
| `-x, --exit_on_failure` | Enable exit on failure mode. |
| `--no-preview` | Skip the preview confirmation prompt. |

## Examples

### Check the downloadable fields

```bash
find_missing_game_metadata
```

### Check only the fields every entry needs

```bash
find_missing_game_metadata -k Minimum
```

### Check every field and show sample entries

```bash
find_missing_game_metadata -k All -v
```

### Report without writing the list files

```bash
find_missing_game_metadata -p
```

## Notes

- Run it from a scratch directory; the report files land in whatever directory you run it from and overwrite earlier ones.
